claims.text: The starting alloy is homogeneous and solution-treated.
The starting alloy has a BCC matrix.
The starting alloy contains no significant secondary phases.
Targeted aging can nucleate and grow fine, coherent B2-ordered nanoprecipitates in the BCC matrix.
Aging at approximately 800–900 °C is an appropriate temperature range for forming the proposed precipitates.
An optimized aging duration can produce uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates without undesirable coarsening.
The resulting structural mediator is a uniform dispersion of coherent B2-ordered nanoprecipitates within the BCC matrix.
Impeded dislocation motion increases alloy strength.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces facilitate dislocation nucleation or absorption.
Interface-assisted dislocation nucleation or absorption maintains or enhances plasticity.
Aging will produce an approximately 20% increase in yield strength relative to the solution-treated reference alloy.
Aging will maintain or slightly enhance ductility relative to the solution-treated reference alloy.
The proposed effect is limited to BCC refractory high-entropy alloys that are capable of forming a B2 phase during aging.
Compositions or aging parameters that do not produce fine, coherent precipitates may fail to improve the strength–plasticity combination.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis says ductility will be enhanced, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained. Maintenance does not establish the claimed simultaneous enhancement of both properties.
